subject: MedBridge HIPAA: data flow & BAA clarifications
messages:
From: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@medbridgehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@medbridgehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifications on PHI in inference pipeline

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and the model-routing capabilities. Before we move to legal, our security and privacy leads asked for a short written clarifying note on a couple of items in your RFI:

1) Does Redwood ever persist PHI (e.g., patient identifiers, notes) outside of customer-controlled storage? If so, where and for how long?
2) Can you describe what metadata is logged at request- and token-level (IP, user_id, prompt hashes, full prompt)? Are any of those considered PHI in your environment?
3) How does your KV/prefix cache behave when requests contain PHI — is that data purged on demand, scoped per-customer, and encrypted?

We reviewed the initial BAA draft and have some redlines, but wanted to get these technical clarifications first.

Could you reply by EOD tomorrow? Attaching the section of our RFI that references these items.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Johnson
Director, Privacy & Security
MedBridge Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@medbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Clarifications on PHI in inference pipeline

Emma —

Really appreciate the clear list. Short answers up top, followed by a concise technical breakdown attached: Redwood_HIPAA_Overview.pdf and a marked-up BAA (Redwood_BAA_Draft_v2.docx).

1) Persistence of PHI: Redwood does not persist customer PHI in any shared or non-customer-controlled long-term store. By default hosted requests may be cached in-memory for short-lived operational purposes (KV cache, prefix cache) to optimize latency; those caches are scoped to customer tenancy and are stored on encrypted volumes or in-memory only. Long-term storage of request/response data only happens if the customer enables logging/retention on their account (audit logs, usage analytics), and that data is stored in the customer partition backed by encrypted S3 and lifecycle policies you control via Console.

2) Metadata logging: Typical logs capture request timestamp, model variant, route, client API key id (token id), region, and anonymized prompt length/sequence statistics. Full prompts are not logged by default in production unless a customer opts into request-level logging for debugging or evals. IPs are recorded in the access logs for security purposes, and are treated as potentially sensitive — we classify IPs as PII and can scope or redact them for PHI-sensitive customers. Prompt hashes (SHA256) are used for deduping cache/telemetry and are not reversible.

3) KV/prefix cache behavior: Caches are per-tenant and have eviction policies based on LRU and sequence length. Customers can opt to disable caching for specific routes or mark routes as PHI-sensitive via the Console API; when marked, we avoid storing user-visible tokens in cache and instead use per-request transient execution with no persistent KV entries. Cache data at rest is encrypted with KMS-managed keys and access is restricted to the serving nodes in that tenant's pool. We also support a purge API to remove cached entries for a tenant on-demand.

A few operational points: audit logs (read/write) are available for Dedicated and Private deployments as part of the standard compliance package; for Hosted we provide a configurable retention (default 30 days) and can negotiate extended retention or reduced verbosity in higher-tier contracts. Breach notification timelines, subcontractor lists, and pen-test cadence are in the attached HIPAA Overview and the BAA redlines.

Attaching: Redwood_HIPAA_Overview.pdf (summary of controls, encryption, logging), Redwood_BAA_Draft_v2.docx (our proposed BAA with comments). Also including a simplified network/dataflow PNG (redwood_network_dataflow.png) in the support docs link.

If you want more detail on specific entries we can set a short technical session with our Security Architect (Marissa) and Legal (Priyom).

Best,

Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Clarifications on PHI in inference pipeline

Thanks Marcus — helpful summary. Two quick follow-ups from our infra lead:

- You mentioned prompt hashes (SHA256) for deduping. Can you confirm no reversible salts or appended metadata allow reconstitution of prompts? Also is the hash tied to customer tenancy or global?
- For the purge API: what's the SLAs for a purge request? Will purge remove entries from all active serving nodes and any analytics indexes? We need assurance purge is comprehensive for PHI removal requests.

Also copied Dr. Reyes to confirm whether they want a short MOP (method of processing) diagram for our compliance team. If Redwood can provide a canned MOP (1–2 pages) that explicitly shows where PHI touches (inference request, optional eval storage, audit logs), that would accelerate review.

Emma

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@medbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@medbridgehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Clarifications on PHI in inference pipeline

Emma — thanks, great questions. Replying with the team cc'd for authoritative answers.

Marissa (Security): can you confirm the hashing process details (no reversible salts, per-tenant salt option, and that hashes are per-tenant by default)? Also please confirm the purge API guarantee (best-effort vs. guaranteed) and an internal SLA we can offer in writing for the BAA: we typically guarantee purge propagation within 24 hours for Hosted when customer retention logging is disabled, and immediate (sub-minute) purge in Dedicated/Private deployments. Please correct if I misstate.

Priyom (Legal): we've attached redlines to the BAA; key commercial asks from MedBridge are limited retention, explicit right to purge, and subcontractor disclosure. Do you want to suggest language for the DocuSign clause and breach notification timelines?

Operational note for Emma/Dr. Reyes: We'll produce a 1–2 page MOP diagram and a short appendix that enumerates exact log fields and the default retention. We can also provide a technical walkthrough with our Security Architect next week.

Action items:
- Marissa to respond with hash/salt and purge SLA statements (security confirmation).
- Priyom to propose revised BAA language and DocuSign flow.
- Marcus to produce MOP 1–2 page and share links.

I'll follow up with calendar invites after Marissa/Priyom reply.

Thanks all,
Marcus
